Addresses that have hard-bounced. The domain-level deliverability check in check_email_domains.py cannot see these: the domain resolves, the MX records answer, and only the MAILBOX is absent. Nothing short of sending finds that out, so once found it must be written down. Keyed by lowercase address. queue_batch.py refuses to send to anything listed here.

Each entry carries a `kind`, which is the useful field: it says what the failure MEANS and therefore what to do next. `no_such_mailbox` -- find another address. `restricted_group` -- an internal-only alias that works for staff and rejects every consumer, so tell the company, because they think it works. `departed_employee` -- the mailbox is fine and the person is gone; use the named successor. `accepts_then_fails` -- the server accepts and only afterwards fails to every recipient, so it LOOKS delivered; do not retry, escalate to whoever is still solvent. `dead_domain` -- check for a re-registration by a stranger before sending anything.

Kinds were backfilled on 2026-08-29 from the free-text evidence of 56 entries that had been recorded as bare strings. The evidence string is preserved verbatim in every case; nothing was rewritten, only classified.

Two further kinds, each recorded once and each meaning something the others do not. `null_mx`: the domain publishes RFC 7505 null MX, an explicit declaration that it accepts no mail at all -- configuration rather than decay, so no amount of retrying or investigating will help. `rejected_ambiguous`: the server refused the message and it is genuinely unclear whether the mailbox is dead or the server is filtering unfamiliar senders; that one is deliberately left unsettled rather than recorded wrongly.

support@calltruth.com.evidence: BROKEN DNS DELEGATION, not a dead mailbox and not a lapsed registration. Gmail gave up 2026-08-28 after three attempts across three days with 'DNS Error: DNS type mx lookup of calltruth.com responded with code SERVFAIL' (status 4.4.3 -- a TEMPORARY code that never resolved). The domain is still registered (eNom, clientTransferProhibited) and still delegated to DNS1-4.NAME-SERVICES.COM, but those nameservers answer SERVFAIL for every record type -- NS, SOA, MX and A -- from two independent resolvers. So this is a third failure shape distinct from the others here: NXDOMAIN means the name does not exist, no-MX-no-A means no mail route, and SERVFAIL means the name is delegated to servers that are broken or gone. Nothing can be delivered and no bounce arrives quickly, because a resolver cannot distinguish a broken nameserver from a briefly unreachable one. Retry only if the delegation is ever seen to answer.
support@calltruth.com.response: The domain itself is gone. Check whether a stranger has re-registered it before sending anything (SILENT_FAILURES 163).
